description: A stereo sample player with six banks of samples it generates itself: modulate the choice of sample and the rhythm falls out of it, with the same clock, pattern generator and oscillator artifex has

params.text: Steps back one bank
Steps on one bank
Attenuates and inverts the voltage at the bank jack; ten volts at full travel is one whole bank
Chooses which sample inside the bank is loaded, from the first at the bottom of its travel to the last at the top
Attenuates and inverts the voltage at the sample jack; modulation that runs past the last sample wraps round to the first, which is what turns a slow ramp into a sequence
Chooses what modulating the sample choice does: play fires a sample the moment modulation crosses into it, so the modulation is the rhythm; cue only aims, and the next trigger fires it
Fires the sample now chosen, by hand
Sets the playback rate, two octaves either way, unquantized
Attenuates and inverts the voltage at both pitch jacks; fully clockwise is exactly one volt per octave
One knob for the envelope and the direction: the shortest envelope at the centre, a growing decay playing forwards clockwise of it, a growing attack playing backwards anticlockwise
Attenuates and inverts the voltage at the length jack
A resonant low-pass closing to 30Hz anticlockwise of the centre, open at the centre, and a resonant high-pass opening to 14000Hz clockwise of it
A delay synced to the tempo, growing wetter anticlockwise of the centre, dry at the centre, and a chorus with soft clipping growing deeper clockwise of it
Chooses whether the oscillator follows the clock, where the rate knob picks a division and the phase is locked to the pattern, or runs free
Sets the oscillator's rate: a division of the clock when it is synced, and its own range when it is free
Attenuates and inverts the voltage at the lfo rate jack
Sets the internal clock, 30 to 300 beats per minute
Chooses one of thirty-two patterns, twenty-two written by hand and ten euclidean distributions over sixteen steps
Writes into the gate pattern as it plays: up randomises the step now passing, down inverts it, the middle leaves it alone
Writes into the CV pattern as it plays: up randomises the level now passing, down inverts it, the middle leaves it alone
Sets the output level
Skews the oscillator's triangle, and since its pulse is high exactly while the triangle rises, the same skew is the pulse's duty cycle

inputs.text: Steps the bank through the attenuverter beside it; ten volts at full travel sweeps the bank once and rests on its last sample, and past that it wraps
Chooses the sample through the attenuverter beside it; in play mode crossing into a sample fires it, and in cue mode it only aims
A rising edge fires the sample now chosen
Bends the pitch continuously as it arrives, through the pitch attenuverter
Sets the pitch as a note: it is quantised to the root and scale chosen on the menu and only read at a trigger, so a sequencer's voltage lands as a note rather than a glide
Added to the length knob through the attenuverter beside it
Added to the lfo rate knob through the attenuverter beside it
A rising edge restarts the oscillator
A clock that takes over from the tempo knob, unless the menu says otherwise
Takes over the gate pattern switch beside it: above its upper threshold randomises the step now passing and below the lower one inverts it
Takes over the CV pattern switch beside it: above its upper threshold randomises the level now passing and below the lower one inverts it
A rising edge returns both the gate and CV sequences to their first step
Sweeps the rhythm across the whole list of thirty-two over ten volts and wraps round

outputs.text: The envelope of the sample now playing
The oscillator's triangle, skewed by the pwm trimmer
The oscillator's pulse, high exactly while the triangle rises
The oscillator's saw, which is its position in its cycle and, synced to sixteen steps, its position in the bar
The running clock passed on, so this module can drive another one's pattern generator and oscillator
The pattern's gate for the step now passing
The pattern's CV for the step now passing
The left side of the sample
The right side of the sample

notes: nothing else needs patching: a trigger and a moving voltage on the sample jack is already a part.
turning the sample knob or stepping the bank is browsing rather than playing. Play mode fires on modulation crossing into another sample, not on a hand moving a control.
one voice sounds at a time: a new trigger chokes the one already playing, which is half of what makes a fast sequence sound tight.
this module and artifex share a clock, a rhythm list, a pattern generator and an oscillator, because on the hardware they are one circuit board with two panels.
at either end of the length knob's travel the envelope is held open and the whole sample plays out, so on the longer banks a sequence becomes a drone rather than a run of hits.
menu: Root — the note the note jack's quantiser is built on
Scale — the scale the note jack's quantiser uses; it affects the quantiser only, and the generated banks are always rendered at C
Reroll kit — a new seed for the six generated banks; the seed is saved with the patch, so a rerolled kit comes back as it was left
Reversed hits decay instead of swelling — off by default; on, a negative length keeps the forward envelope and only the sample is reversed
Reversed hits start at the end of the sample — off by default; on, a reversed hit begins at the last frame and sweeps the whole sample backwards
Reversed hits can retrigger while swelling — off by default; on, a trigger during a reversed hit's attack restarts it instead of being ignored
Sample knob triggers in play mode — off by default, so the knob browses a kit in silence; on, turning it fires each sample it lands on, in play mode only
External clock takes over — whether a signal at the clock jack may take the tempo away from the tempo knob
Pattern input window — the voltage window the two pattern jacks read: 0V neutral, +1V randomize, -1V invert, or Hardware: 1.6-3.2V neutral
Set kits folder… — chooses the folder samples of your own are read from; it is shared with pellicula
Rescan kits — reads that folder again, picking up kits added while Rack was running
Samples per bank — how a kit of your own is cut into banks: 8, which is a generated bank's size, 16, 32, or the whole kit in one
